Data.title: Bitcoin at $10,000? Mike McGlone Warns the Everything Bubble Could Be About to Burst
Data.body: Mike McGlone is sticking to his $10,000 Bitcoin prediction, and his latest post makes it clear he sees trouble far beyond crypto. The Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist believes the market has been running on excess liquidity and speculation for too long. The reversal, now underway, could drag down everything from US stocks and gold to commodities and housing. $10K Nightmare McGlone isn’t ruling out sharp rallies along the way, though he sees them as temporary bursts of optimism in a much deeper bear market. He expects smaller crypto assets, such as Dogecoin, to lose much of their value. Some may even head close to zero. According to McGlone, Michael Saylor-led Strategy could also face serious trouble if Bitcoin’s decline continues. The bigger issue, however, is what happens when the same pressure spreads to traditional markets. McGlone expects the S&P 500 to end 2026 lower, potentially marking its third annual decline since 2009, while metals, energy and other commodities face further downside. The strategist said that falling inflation could pave the way for Fed easing, but believes the damage from years of easy money may still leave investors dealing with a painful correction. His argument is that markets have become so stretched relative to the size of the economy and public debt that a pullback is long overdue. “The trading year of a lifetime is more likely to end like a lion than a lamb.” Arthur Hayes is also expecting more downside, but his $55,000 target is considerably less catastrophic. The BitMEX co-founder believes another test of this level is possible. Hayes was particularly concerned about the weakness in Asian markets. South Korea and Taiwan had already stepped in with emergency measures to support their stock markets, but the selling pressure had yet to ease. Bear Market Not Over Bitcoin’s recovery is looking increasingly shaky. Wintermute had previously said that traders may have mistaken a temporary bounce for a recovery, particularly as the crypto asset fell below its 200-week moving average near $68,000. On the institutional side of things as well, spot Bitcoin ETFs bled nearly $1.8 billion last week. Outflows continued through four consecutive trading days after Monday’s initial inflow. November’s outflows have crossed $4 billion, as institutional investors appear to be losing appetite for the crypto asset at a time when the market desperately needs fresh buying. Wintermute said that “we haven’t cleared the bear market yet, and the rally off the July low was a fake-out.” The post Bitcoin at $10,000? Data.title: €43,000 Crypto Scam: How the Purchase of a Polish VASP Company Led to Lost Money and Vanishing Intermediaries
Data.body: The European crypto market's transition to the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) has changed the operating conditions for companies that previously worked under national registrations. Yet "ready-made" legal entities with legacy Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP) status are still being offered on the market. At first glance, such offers look like a fast track into the European market: an existing legal entity, banking infrastructure, and the appearance of regulatory continuity. But since July 1, 2026, when the MiCA transitional period ended, a legacy VASP status does not by itself replace Crypto-Asset Service Provider (CASP) authorization or confirm the right to provide regulated crypto services. What needs to be verified, therefore, is no longer the old entry in the register but the company's actual legal status. One deal involving the sale of such a company in Poland ended in a €43,000 dispute. After paying, the buyer was not registered as the legal owner of the company and obtained neither corporate control nor the ability to manage the stated banking infrastructure. The money was not returned, and the seller's representatives effectively stopped responding. Who Was Behind the Deal and Where Did the €43,000 Go? At the center of the scandal were Uladzislau Kurban, associated with Iskramentum, and a manager who introduced herself as Michelle Betser. According to the transaction documents, it was Kurban who first made contact with the buyer, after which he handed the negotiations over to Betser, who offered consulting services through the website mbconsulting.me. A look at the intermediaries' digital footprints raised questions that went beyond ordinary commercial due diligence. Michelle Betser's profile turned out to be linked to Olha Sydorenko, also referred to as Sydorenko-Fylypkovska. The documents note matching photographs, contact details, and posts, and, according to the information provided, Sydorenko's LinkedIn profile still contains materials published under the names Michelle Betser and Iskramentum. Olha Sydorenko-Fylypkovska is also linked to Gatwick Advisory Group and Serical Consulting. Allegations against Gatwick Advisory Group have already surfaced publicly: a complaint was posted on LinkedIn about the loss of €15,000 paid for banking services that were never provided. Questions also arise about Kurban himself. His professional LinkedIn profile uses the spelling Władysław Kurban, while the registration information provided lists him as Uladzislau Kurban. The difference may be due to transliteration, but when a financial company is being sold, the identity of its representatives and their authority must be unambiguous. The banking side of the offer raised further questions. The company was sold with an account at Santander Bank Polska, which was renamed Erste Bank Polska in April 2026. The bank itself continued to operate, but the buyer never gained the ability to manage the stated bank account as part of the acquisition. After the final payment, things changed. The company was never transferred, and communication all but stopped. Instead of responses to demands to complete the deal or return the funds, the buyer received mass invitations to book meetings via suspicious links. The lack of proper communication was later blamed on a hacked account. In the end, behind the offer of a ready-made European crypto business stood a chain of intermediaries, professional profiles, and companies with an unclear division of responsibility. Who was the legal seller, who controlled the cryptocurrency payments, and why, once the money was received, were the obligations to transfer the business left unfulfilled and contact lost? Money Received, Business Not Transferred: Who Will Be Held Accountable? The story of the Polish VASP company shows how a deal in the European crypto market can turn into a situation where the money has already been received, the obligations have not been met, and responsibility dissolves among intermediaries, companies, and professional profiles. The questions for Uladzislau Kurban, Michelle Betser, and other participants in the deal now concern not the quality of the services provided, but the possible misappropriation of funds. The use of multiple professional names, opaque business ties, and the absence of any result after full payment make the circumstances of the deal particularly alarming. The buyer in this case paid for an asset that, after MiCA, was already worth little, and never even received it. But the issue goes beyond this particular dispute. As long as the resale of VASP companies stays off regulators' radar and intermediaries can take money without answering for anything, such stories will keep repeating themselves. How this one ends will be decided by law enforcement and the courts. Disclaimer: This article is provided for informational purposes only. It is not offered or intended to be used as legal, tax, investment, financial, or other advice.

Data.title: Cardano voters demand evidence that the Foundation's event tour produced users
Data.body: Cardano’s voting delegates, or DReps, are looking for proof that those who visited booths during the most recent conference tour of the Cardano Foundation actually became users. The delegates look for such evidence before authorizing 24,995,775 ADA for 12 events in 2027. The request has so far been rejected by DReps in charge of 744.05M ADA. Votes in favor carry just 140.94 million ADA. YUTA cast 482.77 million ADA against the 2027 events plan YUTA, the biggest opponent, voted against the withdrawal with 482.77 million ADA. YUTA appraises treasury requests on whether the spending returns “as transactions, fees, or builders who stay.” DRep vote tally on the Cardano Global Events 2027 treasury withdrawal, as shown on CardanoCube on November 23, 2026. YUTA tracked the on-chain transactions of 13 projects that exhibited at TOKEN2049 Singapore in October. The exhibitors’ performance was 1.02 times that of similar projects that did not attend the event, a difference YUTA said was too slight to be distinguished from normal fluctuations. Only 14 of the 293 wallets that received tiny ADA payouts in Paris and Nairobi, according to YUTA, had sent a transaction of their own more than 90 days later. In Nairobi, 54 of the 237 payouts ended up in a single wallet. The pattern suggests that several people submitted more than one claim for the payout, according to YUTA. According to Electric Capital data cited by YUTA, the number of monthly active Cardano developers rose by 8.6%, from 799 to 868, between the year ending in July 2025 and the year ending in July 2026. Increasing the number of new developers by 10% to 15% a year was the aim of the previous events strategy. “I need verifiable evidence connecting previous spending to adoption and real-world usage,” SASA_nagamaru wrote . The same delegate voted No with 130.7 million ADA. BKIND and DeepStatecraft push to stage the 24,995,775 ADA payout The Foundation discusses its events program for 2025-2026 with EMURGO and Rare Network. 8,191 booth contacts and 1,169 developer engagements were recorded by the combined program, and 1,045 individuals registered for the wallet. The program’s goals were either fulfilled or surpassed by all three numbers. One Cardano booth at 12 conferences is what the 2027 proposal calls for. The program includes India Blockchain Week in Bangalore in December and the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi on February 10 and 11. The largest line item in the $4,999,155 budget is $1.99 million for sponsorship packages. The price of ADA in the budget is $0.20. InputEndorsers requests that the Foundation use its own funds to cover the sponsorships. The same delegate also requested an external evaluation of the accomplishments of the previous program. BKIND is against withdrawing all of the funds from the Treasury at once prior to any event. In addition to approving withdrawals that are paid out in stages and verified on-chain, DeepStatecraft would also reconsider a smaller request that is given gradually and linked to conversion objectives. ADA was at $0.15 at the time of writing, up 0.04% from the day before. Following Charles Hoskinson’s announcement this month that the Cardano roadmap was complete, ADA has declined. According to the Foundation, if the price continues to decline, fewer events will be held in the future. The removal of funds from the Treasury requires the support of 67% of the active DRep stake and 2/3 of the Constitutional Committee. The seven members of the committee have not yet cast their ballots. Dec. 20 is the deadline for voting on the action. According to Cryptopolitan , the Foundation gave 11 DReps 220 million ADA in January to more equitably distribute voting power. After a 7.8 million ADA proposal received just 65.2% of the vote, not the required two-thirds, the Foundation called off the 2026 conference in June. If you're reading this, you’re already ahead. Stay there with our newsletter .

Data.title: Why Is Silver Price Surging Today? Silver Jumps 7% as Precious Metals Rebound
Data.body: Key takeaways Silver futures surge 7.2% as precious metals recover Bargain hunting accelerates after last week's market selloff Federal Reserve expectations remain critical for silver prices Silver prices surged on Monday, November 23, 2026, as precious metals staged a sharp recovery following last week's market selloff. Silver futures climbed approximately 7.2% to $44.07 per ounce during the session, while spot silver also recorded strong gains. Why Is Silver Price Rising Today? The biggest catalyst behind Monday's silver rally appears to be renewed buying interest following the metal's recent decline. Silver had fallen sharply alongside gold and US equities as investors reduced exposure to volatile assets. The recovery coincided with an improvement in broader market sentiment, particularly among technology stocks. Silver's historically high volatility helped amplify the rebound, producing larger percentage gains than those recorded by gold. The move also follows a period of significant pressure from higher bond yields and a stronger US dollar. Because silver does not generate interest income, expectations of tighter monetary policy can reduce its attractiveness compared with yield-bearing assets. However, Monday's rebound suggests that traders are reconsidering the extent of the previous selloff. The recovery echoes earlier periods when gold and silver prices responded strongly to changing expectations for monetary policy. Silver Market Faces Sixth Consecutive Supply Deficit Despite recent volatility, silver's underlying supply-demand balance remains relatively tight. According to the Silver Institute's November report , global silver demand is expected to exceed supply by 35 million ounces in 2026, marking the sixth consecutive annual deficit. However, total silver demand is projected to decline 5% to 1.08 billion ounces, while industrial consumption is expected to fall 3%. The contrasting outlook helps explain why the silver market remains sensitive to investor expectations despite persistent supply shortages. The Silver Institute also expects industrial demand outside photovoltaic applications to increase 4.5%, supported by automotive electrification and related infrastructure. This longer-term demand could provide support, although weaker solar consumption remains a concern. Can Silver Price Continue Rising This Week? The next important catalyst is the upcoming US Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation report, which could influence expectations for Federal Reserve interest rates and determine whether silver's recovery continues. A sustained move above $44 could encourage buyers to test the psychologically important $45 level. Conversely, renewed selling pressure could bring the $42 region back into focus, particularly if inflation data strengthens expectations for tighter monetary policy. These levels are potential price scenarios rather than confirmed technical support or resistance. As explored in previous silver price forecasts , interest-rate expectations remain central to XAG/USD movements. Traders will also monitor the gold price outlook for signs that the broader precious metals recovery is gaining momentum.

Data.title: China Stocks Hit 16-Month Low as US Chip Restrictions Threaten AI Rally
Data.body: Key takeaways Shanghai Composite falls to lowest level since July 2025 Chinese semiconductor stocks plunge 5% amid export restrictions New US rules threaten access to advanced AI computing Chinese stocks fell to a 16-month low on November 23 as tightening US semiconductor restrictions and a global artificial intelligence selloff intensified pressure on China's technology sector. The Shanghai Composite declined approximately 1% during morning trading, falling below 3,500 points for the first time since early July 2025. China's CSI 300 Index lost 0.6%, while the semiconductor industry index plunged 5%. Hong Kong stocks also weakened. The Hang Seng Index fell as much as 1.8% to a 19-month low, while the Hang Seng Tech Index, which includes Alibaba and Tencent, reached its lowest level in 26 months. China Semiconductor Stocks Plunge as US Expands AI Chip Controls The latest pressure stems from US efforts to close regulatory loopholes that previously allowed restricted Chinese companies to access advanced processors through overseas data centers. Under a Federal Register rule effective November 19 , the Commerce Department strengthened licensing requirements for certain advanced semiconductor exports and remote computing arrangements. The changes target restricted end users and introduce additional due diligence obligations for data-center operators, chip manufacturers and exporters. These measures expand on earlier US restrictions targeting Chinese AI computing , which placed Nvidia, TSMC and other semiconductor companies under renewed regulatory scrutiny. For Chinese technology firms, the implications extend beyond purchasing chips directly. Companies developing advanced AI models increasingly depend on cloud infrastructure and overseas computing capacity. Restrictions on those arrangements could increase costs and complicate access to high-performance processors. The broader controversy also involves Nvidia's China chip business , which has faced questions about export compliance and potential national security risks. Alibaba and Tencent Face Growing AI Computing Uncertainty China's major technology companies face a difficult combination of restricted computing access, weaker investor confidence and concerns about domestic economic growth. Alibaba and Tencent have invested heavily in cloud infrastructure and artificial intelligence, making access to advanced computing hardware an important consideration for their long-term strategies. Meanwhile, restrictions on American chip exports have renewed interest in China's domestic semiconductor industry. Companies developing locally manufactured AI processors could benefit from substitution demand, although domestic production capacity and access to advanced manufacturing equipment remain constraints. The situation also raises questions for American suppliers. Recent AMD export-control allegations highlighted the scrutiny surrounding semiconductor relationships with Chinese customers. Can China's Stock Market Recover After a 16-Month Low? Chinese authorities have already introduced measures aimed at improving investor confidence. The Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing stock exchanges announced plans to reduce minimum margin financing requirements from 100% to 80%, effective November 30. The change could increase investors' borrowing capacity, but it does not resolve the underlying concerns surrounding technology valuations and access to AI infrastructure. International market conditions present another challenge. Last week's AI stock crash demonstrated how quickly concerns about semiconductor demand and infrastructure financing can spread across global markets. Although Nvidia staged a strong recovery on November 23 following Jensen Huang's reinstatement , Chinese technology stocks remained under pressure during Asian trading.

Data.title: Pundit: XRP Will Melt Faces This Cycle. Watch This If You Are In Doubt
Data.body: Crypto enthusiast Lord XRP has offered XRP holders a reminder of why he believes the cryptocurrency could record significant gains during the current market cycle. In a recent tweet, he encouraged investors who remain uncertain about XRP’s long-term prospects to reconsider Ripple’s expanding connections with financial institutions, government initiatives, and international payment organizations. The tweet included a video presenting several reasons why Ripple could occupy an important position in the future of international payments. IF YOU ARE IN DOUBT HERE IS A SHORT REMINDER TO CALM DOWN #XRP WILL MELT FACES THIS CYCLE pic.twitter.com/C0SW4nKQ4i — Lord XRP (@Bitforcoinz) November 21, 2026 Ripple’s Connections With Global Financial Initiatives The video began by explaining why its speaker holds XRP, describing Ripple as a company positioned to participate in the development of a new global digital payment system that could utilize the cryptocurrency. It traced Ripple’s involvement in payment modernization efforts to 2013, when the Federal Reserve began exploring faster payment options. According to the speaker, the initiative eventually produced an action plan and a federal payments task force that included Ripple as its crypto-focused participant. The speaker also referenced a 2014 report involving the World Bank and the Better Than Cash Alliance. The video connected these organizations to international development initiatives and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals for 2030. It further identified XRP as the cryptocurrency utilized in the Xchange platform’s carbon credit solution, presenting this as another example of Ripple’s involvement in international financial and environmental initiatives. Ripple’s Banking Partnerships and Institutional Connections The video placed considerable emphasis on Ripple’s relationships with established financial institutions. It referenced partnerships involving Bank of America, American Express, PNC, Santander, SBI, HSBC, and Standard Chartered Bank. It also mentioned Ripple’s connections with financial institutions and organizations across Japan, Canada, Egypt, the Middle East, the United Arab Emirates, Thailand, Morocco, Bhutan, South Korea, Brazil, and Latin America. The speaker further connected Ripple to ISO 20022 , the international standard for exchanging electronic messages between financial institutions. The video described Ripple as an early participant in the standard’s development within the distributed ledger technology sector. Former Government Officials and Industry Executives Another major point involved Ripple’s leadership and advisory connections. The speaker referenced former Federal Reserve employees, a former employee overseeing BlackRock’s digital asset division, and individuals with experience in the US Treasury and other government institutions. The video also identified former Federal Reserve attorneys, political advisers, a former German minister, and executives previously associated with SWIFT, PayPal, Uber, Amazon, and the Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation. Additionally, it listed Ripple’s participation in organizations such as the Digital Pound Foundation, Digital Dollar Project, Digital Euro Association, Hyperledger Blockchain Consortium, and World Economic Forum. Lord XRP Maintains His Bullish XRP Outlook The video concluded by questioning whether Ripple and XRP appeared likely to disappear or whether their institutional relationships indicated participation in a much larger financial development. Lord XRP used this presentation to reinforce his confidence in XRP’s performance during the current cycle. His message suggests that investors should consider Ripple’s institutional relationships and involvement in international payment initiatives when evaluating the cryptocurrency’s long-term prospects. Although these connections do not guarantee XRP’s future price performance, Lord XRP remains convinced that the cryptocurrency has considerable upside potential this cycle. Data.title: XRP Price Plunges 25%, but Dom Kwok’s $1,000 Calls Remain in Play
Data.body: XRP is having its worst November on record, but one prominent crypto entrepreneur still sees a four-digit price ahead. EasyA co-founder Dom Kwok has reiterated his $1,000 XRP target for 2030, even as the token crashes toward $0.90 and institutional investors pull money from spot exchange-traded funds (ETFs). XRP has dropped 25% this month, surpassing its previous November record decline in 2019. The token briefly touched $0.862 over the weekend before recovering toward $0.94. It remains below $1, a level XRP has failed to reclaim since November 14. The timing makes Kwok’s forecast look almost absurd on a chart. Yet the sell-off is now testing a level where historical capitulation, ETF positioning, and XRP’s long-term adoption thesis collide. XRP ETFs Are Bleeding, But the Institutional Bet Isn’t Dead The institutional story has taken a serious hit, with spot XRP ETFs recording $30.76 million in November outflows, marking their third consecutive week of withdrawals. Assets across the funds have slipped from around $1.42 billion at October’s end to below $1 billion. November has also produced no daily net inflow for XRP ETFs so far. That is a sharp reversal from the buying streak that helped fuel institutional optimism earlier this year. Still, cumulative net inflows remain near $1.78 billion since launch. Investors have pulled money recently, but the institutional trade has not disappeared. Right now, XRP’s chart is already showing signs of trying to stabilize. The token has bounced from its weekend low around $0.86, with buyers defending the $0.90 area. The daily Relative Strength Index sits near 32, following its recent oversold dip below 30. That is not a confirmed reversal. But XRP does not need a massive catalyst to produce a sharp bounce after a decline this aggressive. Data.title: TCB Daily Edition: What Happened in Crypto on November 23, 2026
Data.body: New announcements on November 23 span exchange security, Bitcoin lending, tokenized securities and stablecoin payments. Strategy and Bitmine also disclosed fresh purchases as major cryptocurrencies rebounded. Bitcoin rebounds above $63,000 as major altcoins recover Bitcoin climbed back above $63,000 during Monday’s trading, extending its recovery from the weekend sell-off. Ether, XRP and Solana also advanced, while Coinbase and Robinhood shares rose alongside a broader recovery in technology stocks. Binance commissions three independent security reviews Binance named Mandiant, SlowMist and Verichains as the outside firms that will examine its security procedures. The exchange said it would use their findings to improve its controls and infrastructure. Monday’s announcement confirmed the appointments; it did not present audit results or conclusions. OKXICE launches round-the-clock tokenized securities trading OKX and NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange announced a venue offering eligible U.S. customers round-the-clock trading in tokenized securities. OKXICE has 113 assets lined up for gradual availability, with each token backed by an underlying share and carrying the associated shareholder rights. The venue operates under a temporary SEC exemption. Strategy adds 457 BTC and expands its buyback program Strategy disclosed that it spent $29.6 million on 457 BTC during November 16–22, bringing its holdings to 851,305 BTC. The company also reported spending $211.8 million to repurchase STRC preferred shares. Its board increased the total authorization for preferred-security buybacks from $3 billion to $4 billion. Bitmine reports another 7,819 ETH purchase Bitmine said its latest weekly purchases added 7,819 ETH, taking its holdings to 6,085,564 tokens as of November 22. The company put that total at approximately 4.98% of ether’s circulating supply. It also reported that more than 5.22 million ETH was staked. Cross River and LendingUSA introduce Bitcoin-backed loans Cross River Bank and LendingUSA launched a program offering eligible borrowers $10,000 to $250,000 against their Bitcoin. Depending on the repayment option, customers can borrow 30%, 50% or 70% of their collateral’s value, with the pledged coins held by a third-party custodian. A decline in Bitcoin’s price can trigger demands for additional collateral or liquidation. American Bitcoin discloses a $150 million FalconX credit line American Bitcoin’s Monday filing revealed a two-year, $150 million revolving credit facility agreed with FalconX on November 18. Borrowings carry a 5.95% annual loan fee and are secured by Bitcoin held with Anchorage Digital Bank. The company had not drawn any funds under the agreement when it filed the disclosure. OCBC and StraitsX pilot stablecoin payments into business accounts OCBC and StraitsX announced a trial allowing participating businesses to receive cross-border payments into their existing bank accounts using stablecoins behind the scenes. StraitsX handles the blockchain payment process, while OCBC provides the banking connection and conversion into conventional currency. NTT DOCOMO Asia is the pilot’s first customer. South Korea prepares to publish its crypto bill draft Local reports on Monday said South Korea’s Financial Services Commission is preparing to publish the government’s Digital Asset Basic Act draft this week. The proposed framework is expected to introduce licensing for crypto businesses and a bank-led model for won stablecoins. It would still need legislative review. Crypto.com adds Veles trading-bot integration Crypto.com Exchange announced that eligible customers can connect their accounts to Veles to automate spot and futures trading. The integration supports dollar-cost-averaging and grid strategies, including testing against historical data. Customers’ funds remain on Crypto.com Exchange while Veles submits trading instructions through an API connection. Zodia Markets announces Jan Brzezek as CEO Zodia Markets announced Jan Brzezek’s appointment as chief executive, disclosing that it took effect on October 14. Brzezek founded Crypto Finance and previously led the business before his move to Zodia. The company also said it had processed more than $25 billion in client trading volume since the start of 2026.

Data.title: DWF Labs: Bitcoin Has Been Falling for 7 Weeks; Weekly Liquidations Total $4.93 Billion
Data.body: Bitcoin recorded its seventh consecutive weekly loss, with damage to leveraged trading intensifying. Weekly liquidations reached $4.93 billion, with $3.75 billion of that coming from long positions, according to a report released today by DWF Labs. Thus, investors expecting a rise accounted for approximately 76 percent of the total liquidations. The report stated that Bitcoin ended the week down 6.88 percent at $60,822, while Ethereum ended with a 6.33 percent loss at $1,718. DWF Labs noted that the last time Bitcoin experienced a sustained decline for seven or more weeks was in the spring of 2022. In the past week, the total cryptocurrency market capitalization also fell by 7.08%, dropping to $2.14 trillion. Related News: Bitcoin Surpasses $64,000: Nvidia CEO’s Decision Boosts Markets Another notable finding of the report was that the sell-off was not limited to cryptocurrencies. In the same-week comparison, the S&P 500 fell 8.6%, and gold dropped 9.5%. DWF Labs’ analysis, dating back to 1979, noted that there is no other instance where gold has experienced such heavy losses in the 42 weeks during which the S&P 500 fell by at least 5 percent. The company attributed the combined sale of different assets to cash flow needs, collateral pressure, and risk mitigation. It stated that it expects volatility to remain high until the market digests the recent move. *This is not investment advice. Data.title: S&P 500 & Dow Jones Price Forecast: Will the Dow Break 50,000?
Data.body: Key takeaways Dow Jones approaches 50,000 after dramatic market rebound Nvidia's comeback lifts S&P 500 and technology stocks Wall Street forecasts point toward further potential gains The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged more than 1,500 points on November 23, bringing the index within striking distance of 50,000 as the S&P 500 staged a powerful recovery from last week's stock market collapse. Around midday in New York, the Dow was trading near 49,655, up approximately 3.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 6.8%. The rally followed a brutal week that sent major US indexes into correction territory. Dow Jones Forecast: Can DJIA Reclaim 50,000? The Dow's November 23 rebound brought the index within approximately 345 points of 50,000, equivalent to less than 1% from its midday level. Crossing the threshold would mark an important recovery milestone, although it would not be a new all-time high. The Dow first crossed 50,000 earlier in 2026 before subsequent volatility pushed it lower. Monday's rally was particularly significant because the benchmark had fallen into correction territory during the preceding selloff. However, the Dow differs from the S&P 500 in an important respect: it is price-weighted rather than capitalization-weighted. That means a dramatic increase in Nvidia's market value does not translate into the same proportional index impact as it does in the S&P 500. For a sustained advance beyond 50,000, investors may need to see stronger participation from financial institutions, industrial companies and consumer businesses. S&P 500 Forecast: Goldman Sachs Targets 8,700 in 2027 The S&P 500 also recovered sharply on Monday, helped by Nvidia's remarkable comeback following Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged more than 30% during the session, extending the earlier 28% premarket rebound . The rebound followed Friday's technology-led market collapse , which pushed the S&P 500 to 6,910.39. Despite the correction, Goldman Sachs maintains a constructive longer-term outlook. In its November market forecast , the bank projected an S&P 500 level of 8,700 for 2027, anticipating continued corporate earnings growth even as the benefits of AI investment begin moderating. From Friday's closing level, that target represents approximately 25.9% potential upside. Morgan Stanley has also identified 8,700 as a possible 2027 destination, reflecting expectations for stronger earnings and improving financial conditions. Its outlook was examined in our earlier Dow Jones market forecast .
